d.why: On screen only in Secret Invasion's Harvest (footage and a photo elsewhere), but he is the MI6 director over Sonya Falsworth, who has a file, and the Skrull mole she shoots and exposes.
Only in Secret Invasion's Betrayed, where he is a boy Fury holds at gunpoint as leverage over the Skrull posing as his father; his father Bob Fairbanks has no file.
On screen in four Secret Invasion episodes (Resurrection, Promises, Betrayed, Harvest) plus a corpse in Beloved.
On screen only in She-Hulk's The Retreat (mentioned in Is This Not Real Magic?), but he is Emil Blonsky's parole officer, the app's boss tie to a filed character, checking his inhibitor.

Only in She-Hulk's Is This Not Real Magic?, where he echoes his friend Donny Blaze as a hype man and agrees to the cease and desist; the case is about Donny, and the wiki calls them friends, not employer and employee.
On screen only in She-Hulk's The Retreat (a photo in Ms. Marvel), where his fight with Man-Bull wrecks Jen's car and he sits in Blonsky's group; a side character in Jen's story.
Only in She-Hulk's finale Whose Show is This?, where he is the AI Jen confronts and whose decision to accept her changes sets how the series ends.

Only in She-Hulk's The People vs. Emil Blonsky (mentioned later), where she is the defendant in Bukowski's suit, the case the episode's second plot is about, and is jailed for impersonating the judge.
On screen only in The Defenders' Mean Right Hook (voice only in episode 1), where he is the missing man Jessica's case is about; his wife Michelle and daughter Lexi have files.
On screen only in The Falcon and the Winter Soldier's The Star-Spangled Man (mentioned in Truth), a Flag Smasher who fights in Munich and leads the oath to Karli, a follower in her story.
On screen only in the Kandahar flashbacks of The Punisher S1 episode 3 (otherwise photo, footage or mentions), where he is the tortured victim whose execution the episode reveals.
On screen in two Punisher S1 episodes, Kandahar and Crosshairs, as Lewis Wilson's father.
Only in The Punisher S1 premiere 3 AM, where he is the young coworker whose involvement in the robbery and near-murder drive Frank to step in and save him.
Only in The Punisher S1's Cold Steel (mentioned once after), one of Russo's hired ex-Anvil gunmen killed in Homeland's warehouse trap; Russo is his boss, not the other way round.
On screen in five Punisher S1 episodes in Curtis's group and with Anvil.
On screen in eight Punisher S1 episodes as David Lieberman's daughter.
Only in The Punisher S1's Crosshairs, where he is the Cerberus colonel Frank hunts at Fort Bryon and Billy then murders, the target the episode is about.
On screen alive in three Punisher S1 episodes (3 AM, Kandahar, The Judas Goat), plus as a corpse in two more.
Only in The Punisher S1 premiere 3 AM, where he is the crew's lead bully who robs the card game and tries to kill Donny, the antagonist Frank kills.
On screen in two Punisher S1 episodes, Front Toward Enemy and Virtue of the Vicious.
Only in The Punisher S1's Cold Steel (mentioned once after), one of Russo's hired ex-Anvil gunmen shot in the warehouse trap; Russo is his boss, not the other way round.
On screen in nine Punisher S1 episodes as David Lieberman's son.
On screen in two Punisher S2 episodes, One Bad Day and My Brother's Keeper.
On screen only in The Punisher S2's Scar Tissue, where Billy visits the group home worker who abused him and kills him in one scene of Billy's story; he is not family or a boss.
On screen in three Punisher S2 episodes as part of Jigsaw's crew.
On screen in The Punisher S2's Trouble the Water, but he is the brother of deputy Ken Ogden, who has a file, and tends Ken's wound during the siege.
Only in The Punisher S2's The Abyss, a morgue worker who shows Karen and Madani three bodies as a favor, a helper in their investigation.
On screen in two Punisher S2 episodes, Flustercluck and The Dark Hearts of Men.
On screen in three Punisher S2 episodes (photo in a fourth) as the senator at the center of the Schultz plot.
Only in The Punisher S2's One Bad Day, a getaway driver in Billy's crew whom Frank shoots; Billy is his boss, not the other way round.
